Canada builds cross-border payment frameworks; execution is now required. 🇨🇦

### Financial Infrastructure & Payments
Canada's ongoing push for real-time rails and expanded non-bank access aims to drastically reduce cross-border settlement costs and friction for corporate entities to hit G20 targets by 2027. Translating policy frameworks into operational connectivity aligns domestic clearing with global ISO 20022 compliance standards. Financial institutions and payment service providers should integrate directly with upcoming real-time rail infrastructure to optimize liquidity and bypass costly intermediary channels.

### Monetary Systems & Digital Assets
The Bank for International Settlements CPMI report highlights that safe, efficient settlement requires combining central bank money with private sector innovations as fast payment systems, stablecoins, and programmable platforms introduce new interdependencies. The Bank of England is providing central counterparties with regulatory clarity to accept tokenised eligible collateral for faster cross-border margin management under the principle of the same regulatory outcome. Market participants and infrastructure providers should build automated collateral mobilisation tools and advise financial institutions on integrating central bank money standards with tokenised platforms.

### Banking Regulation & Governance
Deposit insurers are increasingly adopting expanded mandates that preserve continued access to deposits and related banking services during stress events, aligning closely with modern bank resolution frameworks. Simultaneously, central banks are expanding their operational focus from initial experimentation to comprehensive AI readiness, addressing governance, data infrastructure, and resource allocation. International banking groups and central banks can partner with advisory practices to design liquidity-backed risk management models, compliance workflows, and comprehensive AI readiness audits.
